anatomy: T-Rex: exactly two hind legs, two front arms SHORTER than his head; pterodactyl two legs two wings
motion_rule: the T-Rex acts in every beat and travels with his whole bulk, never talking from a stand; the granny walks into the lens at 4.35 and works huge there to the end; the arms fall short
camera_moves: low angle, ONE continuous take, no cuts, camera always moving: push on the cleaver, arc along the counter, travel with him, low push as she lifts the slab, creep to his snout
character: grumpy old T-Rex butcher, wrinkled hide, enormous head, tiny front arms, stained apron, sleeves rolled up, one white daisy behind his ear
cast: one T-Rex butcher, one granny pterodactyl customer in a headscarf, huge at the lens; nobody else
props: ONE wooden market counter on the ground, one level; a single mound of meat on it; one wooden sign, drawings only: two radishes crossed out, a chicken beside them, no letters no digits; one cleaver
environment: clear noon, open market row, wooden stalls, short grass; dust low
lighting: blazing noon sun overhead, bright throughout, hard crisp shadows, sun through the slab when she lifts it

audio.delivery: gravelly old male voice, market barker, steady 4.5 syllables per second, never hurried
audio.pronunciation: natural native Russian stress, no accent
audio.pacing: one unbroken phrase per window, no pause where a phrase spans two windows, silence in wordless beats, the granny never speaks
audio.lip_sync: jaw works each syllable, mouth free of props while he speaks, voice always from the T-Rex
audio.sfx: cleaver thud 0.0;sign thump into meat 1.5;mound scraping boards 3.65;cleaver bang 4.35;wet poke 5.05;wing flap 6.0;slab slap on counter 8.8

timeline.a: he swings the cleaver down through the mound with his whole bulk behind it, the counter jumping under the blow
he heaves the whole mound round to face camera, apron flapping, rolled sleeves shaking on the tiny arms
he drives the sign into the mound with his foot, stamping it deep; the pictures come up facing the lens
he strides the length of the counter, snout jabbing at the crossed-out radishes, a tiny arm churning air short of them
he drives his whole bulk back down the boards, shouldering the mound along the counter ahead of him
he slams the cleaver into the boards beside the drawn chicken, whole bulk behind it, as the granny walks into the lens, her headscarf filling the frame
he throws his whole bulk back off the counter as she, huge at the lens, pokes one finger deep into the meat
he drives his bulk up the counter after the slab, neck craning, as she lifts it against the sun; the sun burns straight through it, his arms falling short
he drives his bulk down the counter after her, head leading, apron swinging off his chest
he lunges as she slaps the slab back onto the counter; the daisy drops from behind his ear onto the meat and she snatches it, huge at the lens

must_appear: the T-Rex acting in every beat, moving his whole bulk; arms shorter than his head; stained apron, rolled sleeves, daisy behind his ear; ONE counter, one mound of meat; sign: two crossed-out radishes and a chicken; granny in a headscarf huge at the lens from 4.35
